subject: Re: Technical deep-dive & next steps — latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@fintechco.com>, Anand Rao <a.rao@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-20T15:08:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap and technical deep-dive items

Priya / Anand — thanks again for taking time earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery + technical touchpoint and proposed immediate next steps so we’re aligned.

Key pain points you called out:
- Latency spikes during peak trading windows (mkt open +/- 30m) that cause downstream user-visible lag.
- Cost is a top concern — want predictable unit economics while supporting high concurrency.
- Data residency & strict audit requirements for inference logs (must be retained for 90 days, SOC2 evidence requested).

Goals you shared:
- 95th pct latency at or below ~200ms for simple classifying/generation flows; lower is better on critical paths.
- Sustained throughput target: ~1,000–1,200 QPS across the model fleet during peak, with burst to ~1,800 QPS for <5m intervals.
- Support for two model profiles: a smaller fast model for routing/heuristics and a larger high-quality model for long-form responses and sensitive workflows.

Model requirements (as discussed):
- Primary model family: Llama2-style or similar open architecture (you mentioned Llama2-70B as a target for quality).
- Quantized variant acceptable for cost; will need validation on your prompts for quality regressions.
- Streaming output + token-level latencies matter for the UX.

Deployment/topology preferences:
- You indicated preference for a dedicated capacity model (isolated pool) in us-west, with option to move to private (VPC) later for regulated workloads.

Attachments: I’ve attached an architecture diagram and our standard SLA overview for reference (see attachments).

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Rishi — can you provide a technical deep-dive note addressing the latency/throughput targets and suggested deployment topology (GPU types, batching strategy, KV/prefix caching, fallback models)? Target: 48h.
2) Priya/Anand — please confirm the 95th pct latency target (200ms) and the expected average and peak QPS ranges so we can size nodes precisely. Also share any sequence length distributions if available.
3) Schedule a 60-min architecture review with your infra/security team and our solution architects next week.

Thanks — I’ll hold off on sending a formal MLP until we align on the numbers.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap and technical deep-dive items

Marissa — thanks for the concise recap. Confirming the key numbers from our side below so Rishi can size: 

- Latency SLO: 95th percentile <= 200ms for our short-response flows (classification, routing). For long-form generation paths we can accept higher latencies (up to ~800–1,000ms) but prefer streaming.
- QPS: baseline sustained 1,000 QPS across all endpoints; expected peak 1,800 QPS for up to 5 minutes during market open/close.
- Sequence lengths: median token length ~64 tokens for classification/routing; 95th pct up to ~512 tokens for long-form journeys.
- Concurrency: expect ~450 concurrent active users during peak, with many parallel inference calls per user (hence the QPS numbers).

Model preferences: Llama2-70B as the high-quality model; a quantized 8-bit or 4-bit variant is acceptable for cost if output quality is validated against our evaluation prompts. We also want a smaller ~7B variant for quick heuristics and routing.

Security/compliance: we need audit logs for 90 days, role-based access for predictions and keys, and SOC2 evidence. We’ll share a short questionnaire with our security team by EOD.

Next: happy to join an architecture review next week. Our security lead (Anand CC’d) will also be present. Please propose 2 slots and we’ll confirm.

Thanks,
Priya
Head of AI Integrations | FinTechCo
priya.shah@fintechco.com | +1 212-555-0199

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Anand Rao <a.rao@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-02-21T10:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Technical sizing and proposed deployment topology (deep dive)

Priya / team — thanks for the confirmation. Below is a technical deep-dive with concrete sizing and options based on the numbers you provided. This note is focused on meeting the 95th pct latency <=200ms for short flows while supporting peak QPS bursts.

Summary of assumptions (from your inputs):
- 95th pct latency target: 200ms for short flows (median ~64 tokens)
- Sustained throughput: 1,000 QPS; peak bursts to 1,800 QPS (<=5 minutes)
- Sequence length: median 64 tokens, 95th 512 tokens
- Model mix: 7B variant for routing (fast path) + 70B for high-quality responses

Recommended topology (primary): Redwood Dedicated — isolated GPU pool in us-west-2, reserved nodes for steady state + burst cluster for peak handling. Private (VPC) deployment is a follow-on once procurement completes.

Hardware recommendation:
- Steady-state: 8 x A100 80GB (or equivalent) nodes configured with persistent KV cache and continuous batching tuned for low-latency small sequences. These handle the baseline ~1,000 QPS when we run a mixed fleet (routing 7B + fallback 70B for heavy requests).
- Burst capacity: autoscaling pool made of p4d or equivalent (A100) instances that can add ~6–10 nodes within 90–120s to cover burst to 1,800 QPS.

Batching and latency strategy:
- Continuous micro-batching with adaptive target batch sizes: for short sequences we aim for batch sizes that keep token-broadcast latency <25ms per token (this helps hit 200ms total for the end-to-end short flows).
- Prefix/KV caching: we’ll enable prefix caching for repeated contexts to shave 30–60% of tokens on common paths. We’ll instrument cache hit rates and can recommend cache TTLs after seeing real traffic.
- Dynamic routing: route heuristic/routing calls to the 7B pool (local) and high-quality requests to the 70B pool; automatic fallback to quantized 70B variant if latency is trending above threshold.

Model & quantization notes:
- 70B quantized (4-bit/8-bit) is feasible; we’ll validate quality on your eval prompts. We recommend keeping a small subset of requests on a FP16 or 8-bit high-precision variant during initial rollout for accuracy comparisons.

Estimated latency profile (ballpark):
- 7B routing model (median 64 tokens): 95th pct ~80–150ms depending on batching and cache hit rate.
- 70B quantized (median 64 tokens, with caching): 95th pct ~160–300ms — with careful kernel selection and GPUs above, we can target the lower end (<=200ms) for many requests, but long-form 512-token journeys will be higher (streaming recommended).

Operational / compliance:
- We can enable 90-day audit log retention and integrate with your KMS for key management. SOC2 artifacts: we’ve attached a checklist and can provide the evidence package during the security review.

Open questions / items needed from FinTechCo to finalize sizing:
1) Typical payload sizes (bytes) and distribution of request vs streaming responses.
2) Confirmation on max tolerated cold-start windows for elastic nodes (we estimated 90–120s).
3) Any strict limits on GPU SKUs or cloud providers for procurement.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Schedule the 60-min architecture + security review (I can run through the sizing and the audit artifacts).
- After review, we’ll deliver a formal MLP (minimum launch plan) with pricing, node counts, and an inferred SLA for the dedicated pool.

Happy to sync live — proposed times: Tues 2026-02-24 09:00–10:00 PST or Wed 2026-02-25 13:00–14:00 PST.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
